title: De altitudine columnarum sub proprio pondere corruentium

errors: No mathematical error: both arm equilibria give ½Ca + Maθ = 2Eeθ, and the critical condition Ma = 2Ee is correct for this pinned two-link model with a rotational spring at mid-height.

Euler says the formula needs Ee to be 'much greater' than Ma so that θ is small. Strictly, the linearised formula only needs θ to be small, which can also hold near the critical load when C is small enough; the remark is heuristic.
Misprint in the original: 'vim horizontalem Ce = C' should read Cc = C.

ideas.what: Rigid two-link column with an elastic rotational spring at mid-height, used to find the critical self-weight load
ideas.modern_name: Discrete rigid-bar/spring buckling model (Hencky bar-chain / Shanley-type model)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Discrete link models are usually associated with 20th-century stability theory (Hencky 1920; Shanley 1947). Euler's own use in E510 is discussed in histories of elasticity.
ideas.where_published: E510 itself (Acta Acad. Sci. Petrop. 1778, publ. 1780); discussed by Truesdell (1960, Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies, Opera omnia II 11/2)

ideas.what: Critical load defined as the load at which a deflection needs no lateral force, so θ becomes indeterminate
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (1744 Additamentum on elastic curves; 1757 E238)

ideas.what: Deflection under a lateral load C with weight present: θ = Ca/(4Ee − 2Ma) = θ0/(1 − Ma/2Ee)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thomas Young (1807) for the eccentric/imperfect column; Ayrton–Perry (1886)
ideas.where_published: Implicit only in this formula; Euler does not write it in factored form

ideas.what: Critical height of a heavy column, b = √(8Ee/dd) (next page), contradicting Euler's earlier view that no column collapses under its own weight
ideas.modern_name: Self-weight buckling height (discrete approximation; exact continuum result by Greenhill 1881)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Greenhill (1881) for the continuous case; Euler 1778 attempts
ideas.where_published: E510 (and the companion papers E508, E509)

missed.claim: Euler's lateral-load formula is precisely the beam-column amplification law, θ = θ0/(1 − N/Ncr), for a discrete model, about 30 years before Young (1807). Euler uses it only to locate the singularity and never states the magnification interpretation, so this is at most a minor priority note.
missed.quote: erit enim θ = Ca/(4Ee − 2Ma); ... erit enim ista vis C = (2θ/a)(2Ee − Ma)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A small historical precedent for the amplification factor and for the imperfection/lateral-load approach to the critical load. Specialists in the history of stability theory may not have attributed this to Euler.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a correct, careful discrete buckling model inside a paper historians (Truesdell, Todhunter–Pearson) already know. The only mildly unrecognised feature is that the formula has the amplification-factor form, which Euler does not exploit.
transcription_corrections: The transcription matches the image well. 'Ce = C' is faithful to the print but is a misprint for 'Cc = C'.
The transcription's long-s forms are inconsistent ('finiftrorfum', 'eft', 'fiue' alongside 'suppo-'); the original uses long s (ſ) throughout.
